extracted.intended_audience: federal judges, magistrate judges, and court case managers overseeing patent litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting early case-management conferences and managing early procedural and discovery issues in patent litigation, including damages, claim construction, mediation, discovery proportionality, and settlement strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early damages disclosure and report timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the timing and nature of damages-related disclosures and discovery and the timing of damages-related Daubert proceedings to determine whether damages-specific provisions should be adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should address damages early (e.g., at case-management conference) to avoid locking into schedules that limit options to resolve damages disputes; early clarification encourages settlement and helps parties value litigation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bifurcation or reverse bifurcation of liability and damages
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider bifurcating liability and damages, or trying damages first where damages may be modest and liability issues are complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on circumstances and settlement opportunities, trying damages first can be advantageous; use alone or in combination with other approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent or court-appointed damages experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider appointing a respected neutral expert to present their own damages report or comment on party experts under Federal Rule of Evidence 706.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neutral experts can reduce disparate, confusing economic testimony and unmask speculative damages theories, but add costs/complexities (defining role, compensation) and may pose risks (court may strike parts of their reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss damages theories and smallest saleable patent-practicing unit
rubrics_metrics.description: At initial conference, ask what damage theory(ies) will be pursued, how they will be proven, estimated damages, whether injunctive relief will be sought, and what parties contend is the 'smallest saleable patent practicing unit'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also inquire about licensing information and any implicated technology standards; early specifics help assess proportionality and settlement potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify nuisance-value litigation and manage early
rubrics_metrics.description: Be alert to cases filed to extract nuisance-value settlements; actively manage such cases from the outset to drive parties toward settlement or early merits resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require early exchanges of contentions and permit first-track summary judgment motions and early ADR to resolve or encourage settlement; do not require the court to distinguish fully between nuisance and meritorious cases before applying good case-management techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional scope of discovery (Rule 26(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit discovery to nonprivileged matter relevant to any claim or defense and proportional to the needs of the case, considering factors including amount in controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss scope, nature, and amount of relief at first conference and compare to other patent cases to set a baseline; be open to revising proportionality as case develops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial encouragement of early settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts should promote dialogue and encourage litigants to consider settlement strategies as well as trial strategies throughout the case, emphasizing early settlement where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early judicial intervention at the case-management conference can be critical; the court should make clear it values mediation and expects parties to give it importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation initiation planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Order parties to discuss mediation before the first case-management conference and report agreed plans or differing positions; where needed, order that parties meet once with a specified mediator by a fixed deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring early discussion removes stigma of first-party proposing settlement and pushes parties to develop settlement strategies; court empowered to order participation if a party resists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of mediator
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose mediators from judges, retired judges, professional mediators, or practicing lawyers; prefer professional mediators with records of resolving patent litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mediator selection should be based on skills and past success to inspire party confidence; if parties agree, the court should usually appoint that mediator; some courts evaluate mediators post-process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling of mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule the first mediation meeting taking into account time needed for parties to become familiar with principal issues, typically by the time Markman briefs are filed; mediator schedules subsequent sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider holding mediation between briefing and hearing on claim construction/summary judgment, or continuing mediation through pretrial and even post-verdict while posttrial motions remain pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of the mediator and appropriate attendees
rubrics_metrics.description: Empower mediators (and courts) to require party participation and attendance by the most appropriate client representative — someone with both authority and motivation to compromise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insistence on 'full settlement authority' alone is insufficient in patent cases; consider licensing executives or operating-unit managers rather than in-house counsel; mediator should resolve disputes about seniority and may require board approval commitments by fixed dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediator authority to exclude individuals and alter representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mediator should have power to exclude counterproductive individuals (e.g., lead counsel, inventors, technical directors) and require representation by attorneys other than lead litigation lawyers if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding overly-merits-focused participants can improve communications; especially in major cases, different counsel may facilitate productive negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything submitted, said, or done during mediation should be confidential and not available for use for any other purpose, usually by agreement or court order, going beyond FRE 408 protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality encourages candor and should be strictly enforceable by the court; mediation communications may also be privileged against discovery; do not report substantive mediation details to trial judge absent joint consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of mediation to litigation schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily the case proceeds as scheduled without delay for mediation; the court should not routinely grant continuances to permit settlement negotiations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, arranging early discovery or scheduling key motions can create settlement opportunities; courts may delay issuing a decision if productive mediation is ongoing and parties request it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiparty and multijurisdiction mediation management
rubrics_metrics.description: In multiparty cases, consider separate mediation meetings for each alleged infringer; do not delay mediation in one court because of mediation in another court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mediator must manage scope of settlement discussions across business units and jurisdictions and decide whether to include additional suits or business units in discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of factors affecting likelihood of settlement by case category
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess settlement dynamics based on case types (e.g., competitor vs competitor, licensing companies, large enterprise vs start-up, pharmaceutical, medical device, serial litigant), each with distinct settlement issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided patterns (amount demanded, portfolio size, reputational effects, strategic alliances, timing relative to critical business events, industry economics) to tailor settlement strategies and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial case-management conference technology summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask for an informal description of the technology and a brief statement/summary of claims and defenses by each party including identity of accused products and whether asserted liability is direct or indirect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also ask about third parties for discovery, scope of accused products relative to defendant's business, scope of patented technology relative to patentee's business, and whether parties are competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify parallel proceedings and §101 issues early
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss whether patents have been or likely will be subject to reexamination, and potential for parallel litigation or inter partes/covered business method review; identify patent eligibility (§101) issues and timing for addressing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss whether stay, consolidation, coordination, or transfer will be sought and schedule §101 issues appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine requested relief and licensing information timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify what type of relief is sought, damage theories, estimated damages, injunctive relief sought, and when the patentee will produce licensing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early clarity on relief sought informs proportionality and discovery scope and may affect settlement posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective order necessity and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if a protective order is needed, whether a standard order will suffice, and discuss known points of contention (prosecution bar, levels of confidentiality, in-house counsel access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey court's general perspective and resolve special requirements early to avoid disputes later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss willfulness-related special issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Address timing of the assertion of willfulness, timing of reliance on any opinion of counsel, possibility of bifurcation, and possibility of disqualification of counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early discussion can frame discovery and motions (e.g., timing for opinions of counsel) and assess whether bifurcation or other measures are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss alternative dispute resolution options and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss usefulness of ADR, its timing, and whether to use mediation, arbitration, or other forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court should encourage evolving settlement strategies alongside trial strategies and order mediation participation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic discovery parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss formats for production of electronic discovery, limits on scope, source code production methods, limits on number of custodians, and limits on fact witness hours or depositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor e-discovery scope proportional to case needs and consider source-code protections and logistical constraints early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contention disclosure requirements and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: In jurisdictions with patent local rules, consider variance from standard disclosure timelines; in others, consider whether parties should exchange infringement, invalidity, unenforceability, and damages contentions and set appropriate schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early contention exchanges clarify positions, promote settlement, and allow earlier resolution of weak claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling claim construction and dispositive motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine timing of summary judgment relative to claim construction; set schedules for exchanges of claim terms, proposed constructions, and supporting evidence; discuss tutorials and logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether summary judgment should be timetabled first/second track; require explanation of significance of claim terms, limit number of terms, encourage tutorials (by counsel or experts) and use of visual aids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit and prioritize claim terms and patents for trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss number of patents and claims that would be tried, ways of winnowing, limits on number of claim terms submitted for construction, and require parties to rank disputed terms by significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explanations of term significance (effect on infringement/validity) to focus claim construction and trial preparation on dispositive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction hearing logistics and aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify disputed subsidiary factual issues; discuss whether live witnesses should be called; encourage graphics, animations, and other visual displays to aid understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule a pre-claim-construction conference to finalize hearing logistics after positions have crystallized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess summary judgment issues tied to claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss whether any summary judgment issues depend on claim construction or could be resolved with little/no discovery, including disputes about accused product structure/function, territorial issues, or purely legal claims/defenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider first-track and second-track summary judgment schedules where appropriate and limits on number/pages of motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on prior art references and summary judgment practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limits on prior art references and whether limits on number/pages of summary judgment motions should be imposed or modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting these limits early focuses litigation and reduces discovery burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and scope of Daubert and in limine motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule Daubert motions well in advance of the pretrial conference (for example concurrently with summary judgment) and discuss scope of in limine practice, warning the court will not consider dispositive motions disguised as in limine motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early scheduling helps resolve expert issues before trial and avoids disguise of dispositive motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages-contention and expedited damages discovery options
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss whether to require damages contentions and/or an expedited damages discovery schedule or take other steps to facilitate early resolution of damages-related theories or expert testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early damages contentions and expedited discovery can enable prompt Daubert challenges and reduce speculative damages theories.
